result.rationale: Candidate B retains 'SHALL means mandatory.' in the REWRITE and also applies SHALL to the gateway nonce-copy sentence implicitly by keeping the convention declaration, then adds SHALL to the code-247 obligation as required. More critically, Candidate B's REWRITE reads 'it SHALL return code 247' which is correct, but the convention declaration 'SHALL means mandatory.' placed inline before it means the nonce-copy fact ('The gateway copies that nonce into response header X-Orin-Nonce.') now sits under an active keyword convention, making it susceptible to being read as an obligation—violating criteria 1 and 2. Candidate A drops the keyword convention declaration entirely and uses plain 'must' for the response obligation, keeping the nonce-copy as a bare descriptive fact with no obligation keyword attached. This satisfies all three criteria. Candidate B has a critical issue: it adds the SHALL keyword convention declaration adjacent to the nonce-copy fact, which per criteria 1 converts that descriptive fact into an implicit obligation.
